underlines.text: Had I been in love, I could not have been more wretchedly blind.

reference.text: Darcy nor Wickham could she think, without feeling that she had been blind, partial, prejudiced, absurd.

underlines.text: Pleased with the preference of one

reference.text: His behaviour to herself could now have had no tolerable motive: he had either been deceived with regard to her fortune, or had been gratifying his vanity by encouraging the preference which she believed she had most incautiously shown.

underlines.text: Mr. Darcy’s explanation there had appeared very insufficient

reference.text: With a strong prejudice against everything he might say, she began his account of what had happened at Netherfield.

underlines.text: Widely different was the effect of a second perusal.

reference.text: She read with an eagerness which hardly left her power of comprehension; and from impatience of knowing what the next sentence might bring, was incapable of attending to the sense of the one before her eyes.

underlines.text: the justice of his description of Jane

reference.text: His belief of her sister’s insensibility she instantly resolved to be false; and his account of the real, the worst objections to the match, made her too angry to have any wish of doing him justice.
